confidence_explanation: The evidence shows a clear pattern of session hijacking followed by unauthorized cross-departmental data exfiltration. The mid-session IP change is a definitive indicator of a hijacked session, and the subsequent actions (accessing HR, DevOps, Engineering, Finance, and Sales directories) are entirely outside the user's baseline.

attack_chain.description: User_09 logs in from their normal IP (192.168.1.109) during normal hours.
User_09 performs legitimate file reads within their own marketing directory.
Session hijacking occurs: the same session_id (sess_user_09_20260709_001) is used from a new, external IP (91.219.236.222), and the user begins accessing HR files.
Attacker downloads DevOps runbooks from the shared directory.
Attacker downloads Engineering project files from the shared directory.
Attacker downloads Sales draft documents before logging out.

gaps: Information regarding the nature of the external IP (91.219.236.222) to confirm if it is a known malicious actor or VPN.
Logs from the authentication provider to see if there were any MFA bypasses or credential theft indicators.
narrative: A session hijacking incident occurred where user_09's session was hijacked mid-session, evidenced by a sudden IP change from 192.168.1.109 to 91.219.236.222. The attacker used this hijacked session to perform unauthorized cross-departmental data exfiltration, downloading sensitive files from HR, DevOps, Engineering, Finance, and Sales directories.
